methods_notes: A rigorous Sources & Method page must state: (1) MPDF DRAFT STATUS — the dataset's backbone, Marx & Jaffke's Northern California Doghole Ports Maritime Cultural Landscape MPDF (CA DPR/OHP), is cited as a DRAFT multiple-property nomination; its inventory numbers, page numbers, and even inclusion decisions can change before listing, and eight features (northport, pallas-bay, bromley-gulch, big-gulch, henleys, chisholm, joe-tongues, stockhoff-cove) rest on bare 'X, via the MPDF' strings with no URL — i.e., primary sources (Davidson pages, Clark, Rudy, Carranco & Labbe, T-sheets) quoted at second hand and never independently opened. The page must distinguish 'read directly' ([P] tags) from 'inherited from the MPDF inventory.' (2) COAST PILOT DATE LAG — Davidson 1869 reflects field reconnaissance of c.1867-69 and the 1889 4th edition field data of c.1885-87; a port 'active' or 'abandoned' in the 1889 text is dated to the survey, not the imprint, and ports founded after ~1887 (Notley's 1898, Mattole wharf 1908, Walsh's 1889+) are structurally invisible in it — absence from Davidson is not evidence of absence. Post-1889 landings need the 1903/1909/1917 US Coast Pilot, which is not on archive.org (verified: only Atlantic/Alaska/Philippine volumes) and is cited in this dataset only at second hand via NOAA. (3) FOUR-TIER CLASSIFICATION BASIS — the chute-only/pier/river-bar/deepwater tiers must each name their evidentiary warrant: the doghole vessel-size/tonnage ceiling from Walter A. Jackson, The Doghole Schooners (1977; catalog record verified, OpenLibrary OL4449329W — not online, so the methods page must give the catalog record); pier vs chute assignments from MPDF inventory structure counts and Davidson's loading descriptions; river-bar practice from the HAER No. CA-61 (C.A. Thayer) data pages on bar-harbor passage (loc.gov/item/ca1201); deepwater status from engineered-harbor evidence (Humboldt jetties per Magoon et al., ICCE). State that a class resting on a single T-sheet or one adjectival phrase carries lower confidence, and that the classification of ports with no surviving structure description is inferential. (4) COORDINATE PROVENANCE — the JSON's coord_precision vocabulary ('place', etc.) must be defined with an error radius and a per-feature provenance regime: T-sheet/Coast Pilot bearing, GNIS name, or visual aerial placement; cliff-edge doghole sites shift interpretation materially at 100 m error. (5) COVERAGE ASYMMETRY — Mendocino/Sonoma features inherit a dense professional apparatus (MPDF, NOAA GFNMS pages, Fort Ross research design, Palmer 1880); Humboldt/Del Norte lean on Bearss and county histories; Marin, San Mateo, Santa Cruz, Big Sur, and SLO features were assembled from museum blogs, visitor bureaus, Wikipedia, and hobby sites. Uniform symbology masks a non-uniform evidence base — publish a per-feature source-tier field (primary-read / primary-via-secondary / tertiary-only). (6) SUPERLATIVES POLICY — 'highest and longest' (Needle Rock, from an 1898 Chronicle item quoted in the MPDF) and kindred first/largest claims must stay attributed to their newspaper-era sources, never flattened to fact. (7) LINK ROT AND ACCESS — the NPS parkhistory online_books URLs for Bearss (cited at four features) now redirect to a generic Park History page (verified); cite Wayback snapshots with capture dates. FoundSF is blocked to scripted fetch (already flagged in-dataset); Calisphere is bot-blocked (leads only); IA lending books (Cox, Shanks, Stindt, Hamman, Gordon, Henson) verify at catalog level but resist page-level remote verification. (8) PHOTO RIGHTS REGIME — state explicitly that MCMRHS, Kelley House, HMDB, lighthousefriends, and news-site images are NOT cleared for reuse and that the map embeds none of them; HABS/HAER, NOAA, NPS, and USCG images are US-government public domain; pre-1930 county-history plates are public domain; Arcadia and UC Press illustrations remain in copyright. (9) One factual correction found in passing: the mattole feature's [P] Davidson cite says 'p. ~280' but the Mattole/Punta Gorda text sits at ~pp. 300-301; a systematic page audit of all [P] Davidson cites has not been run and should be disclosed as pending.

(3) The Pacific-coast 1909/1917 US Coast Pilot — the missing primary for post-1889 landings (Notley's, Fields Landing, Walsh's) — was not found on archive.org; HathiTrust should be checked next.
